<span id="paper-post-training-ask-to-distill-6c38407f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-037eb7aa83d997b6">Why train an A2D question synthesizer before training student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Questions determine visited prefixes and usable guidance. Freeze scorer teacher/student, optimize question distribution, screen pool then distill from original student. Separate curriculum learning from student gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Find learnable challenge problems without accumulating student updates while selecting them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-037eb7aa83d997b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdbf7cacadf7e6e0">Why require disagreement and teacher support within student reach?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement alone can choose unlearnable problems, compatibility alone mastered ones. Reward their product using raw teacher mass, freeze scorers, then distill from original student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher refinement near two known approaches has useful gap; mass almost entirely off-support should score low.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdbf7cacadf7e6e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-694dff9b34d8b000">How does A2D compatibility differ from pure disagreement reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A big gap can mean impossible. Compatibility measures teacher mass on student support. Product balances room for learning and reachability rather than reward distance alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher-only path can have high disagreement but poor teachability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-694dff9b34d8b000">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-403dedcf6fb8e94d">Why not renormalize A2D compatibility on the candidate union?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use raw full-vocabulary teacher mass on student candidates; renormalization hides mass outside. Deduplicate across complete scoring batch, not one GRPO group; don&#x27;t arbitrarily restandardize downstream advantages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher mostly supports inaccessible tokens, local normalization overstates compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403dedcf6fb8e94d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tar-adaptive-replay-2e44ae67" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-58ca00fbe8a70481">Why collect actual correct base samples for TAR memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recover modes base could truly generate and current training suppresses. Generate, verify with training-only checker and choose diverse prototypes. No correct samples means no bank; hand-written gold is not reachability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A never-generated base solution cannot be labeled a forgotten skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58ca00fbe8a70481">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ebca3f0a5ff34c64">Why replay only correct traces suppressed relative to base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verified real base samples store diverse reachable solutions. Gate inactive if unchanged; if suppressed, concentrate on lowered tokens. Detached selection prevents optimization through the gate, and test labels are excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restore disappearing algebra steps without repeatedly forcing a still-common diagram solution or inventing archived samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ebca3f0a5ff34c64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-267997e69aa769dd">How does adaptive TAR differ from repeated SFT on fixed archive?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open the gate only when relative-to-base suppression occurs, focusing suppressed tokens. Fixed replay always supervises, potentially constraining new adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skip a still-common old solution until its likelihood falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-267997e69aa769dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32e3a7b26d024e5">May TAR average only active gate trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divide by all bank traces, including zero gates. Detach gate/token weights and use stable mixed precision. Active-only normalization amplifies rare activation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If just one trace is suppressed, active-only averaging makes it stronger than the bank mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32e3a7b26d024e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stopd-818867f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ade71d0b770864e">Why choose STOPD cutoff randomly before generating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent advance sampling defines each position&#x27;s inclusion probability and saves actual generation. Trimming after generation only saves supervision and can bias selection. Natural EOS remains valid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose a block cutoff before seeing the answer, not the most favorable length afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ade71d0b770864e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-986fe23827dbb58a">Why not normalize inverse-probability gradients by current random token count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late positions are less observable and inverse probabilities debias the sum. Dividing by a correlated random denominator needn&#x27;t preserve expectation. Use previous weighted count, detached along with weights. Nonlinear optimizer steps still differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Upweight seldom-observed later steps without claiming one short average equals full generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-986fe23827dbb58a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba0afc9a512a246e">Does inverse-inclusion weighting make each Adam step identical?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The weighted gradient sum can match full-sum expectation, but normalization and nonlinear optimizer state matter. It is not per-batch update or final-training equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two short draws may average toward the full sum while giving different adaptive steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba0afc9a512a246e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb36605b4b19c6d7">How handle partial final blocks and STOPD normalizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use exact coverage probabilities for the short tail and previous batch&#x27;s weighted count as current normalizer. Keep begin/loss/finish lifecycle against reuse. Do not replace with current random count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A maximum length not divisible by block width still has exact tail probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb36605b4b19c6d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-synthself-6e723ecb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a53b09934bf1fdde">Why use a larger same-family SynthSelf rewriter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small self-rewrites can distort content and original style may be difficult for students. A larger aligned rewriter supplies candidates verified by answer checks; shorter isn&#x27;t automatically better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Convert a proof with skipped steps into learnable steps while retaining the correct result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a53b09934bf1fdde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2403206d644220f">Why rewrite with a larger related model and check the answer again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can adapt training demonstrations to students but may introduce mistakes. Accept through answer checking and test fidelity/distribution requirements. Do not use evaluation answers to rewrite or condition the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify that a simplified solution reaches the same conclusion; using test solutions invalidates generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2403206d644220f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a15e41148b5baa0">How does answer rejection sampling differ from validating format?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid structure does not ensure correctness. Check rewritten answers, then test distribution/fidelity constraints empirically. Same family guarantees neither.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A syntactically correct JSON result with wrong arithmetic should be rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd88b8babcbee15a">Where may SynthSelf use gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline training demonstrations can guide and validate rewrites. Never give evaluation answers to student or use them for curriculum. Real SFT remains necessary; preserve failed and repaired evidence separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text filtering without a parameter update isn&#x27;t complete training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-progressive-contraction-16120d48" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7b2e9d5c5821ab1">Why select high branching uncertainty among correct trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct endings can hide fragile branch points. Monte Carlo continuations identify teachable states beyond binary original correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proof with confusing mid-course formula options is useful despite a correct ending.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7b2e9d5c5821ab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-99594692ebd73c81">Why profile teacher branch uncertainty, then select by student loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Monte Carlo continuations identify fragile points on correct traces; shrink by teacher profile, then probe students and train on current high-loss items. Rerouting follows learning. Reduced student exposure is not end-to-end speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a fragile proof first and switch after mastery; correctness alone cannot choose.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99594692ebd73c81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a24601f33c222bf6">What do teacher profiling and student NLL rerouting each solve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher stage finds potentially difficult reasoning states; student probes find current gaps. Teacher difficulty isn&#x27;t permanent student difficulty and isn&#x27;t length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move budget if the student already mastered a teacher-profiled difficult step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a24601f33c222bf6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b729b9b90aee1d77">Why doesn&#x27;t reduced exposure imply equivalent total GPU acceleration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposure counts student training only, omitting real teacher profiling, probes and overhead. Log separately and keep evidence of generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Expensive screening may outweigh two fewer training epochs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b729b9b90aee1d77">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grpo-difficulty-curriculum-3b9ce14e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3963a5ac4b91e90">Why does GRPO curriculum difficulty change as policy improves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Measure difficulty through current sampled pass rate; learning and forgetting move items between bands. Static text length or old scores aren&#x27;t the same.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Yesterday&#x27;s failed short prompt can become easy today.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3963a5ac4b91e90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff387fdac665f742">Why remeasure success instead of using fixed question length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Difficulty is policy- and budget-dependent, so real-rollout success bands shift with learning. Select phases on validation and retain hard-stage controls; length reward doesn&#x27;t replace difficulty or justify test selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short arithmetic problem may be harder for current model than a familiar long problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff387fdac665f742">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0bcbab33c779c96">Why isn&#x27;t online fixed-medium equivalent to progressing to hardest band?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed-medium preserves learnable success rates. Hardest progression can lose signal, and reported hardest-stage regression should remain visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A curriculum crossing capability may yield only failures rather than progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0bcbab33c779c96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf468dcf604fdc63">May phase selection use test scores or length reward to define difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Select by validation, restore selected checkpoint and reestimate pass rates from actual current rollouts. Length reward is auxiliary, not difficulty. Static mock rates aren&#x27;t online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long output alone does not make a problem hard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf468dcf604fdc63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-branch-opd-974c9738" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b4958bb5fa31a4">Why sample extra suffixes at uncertain BranchOPD forks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One rollout shows only one continuation. Frozen student branches expose multiple choices at the same state, focusing teacher supervision on disagreement rather than teacher-selected text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try two continuations independently from the same proof prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b4958bb5fa31a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6570a1154693895c">Why count shared prefix only once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branching widens continuations, not earlier supervision. Select uncertain/disagreeing forks and sample independent frozen-student suffixes for teacher scores, without teacher forcing or gold filters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Count three shared steps once, then each of two suffixes separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6570a1154693895c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-773ea46ef6380052">How does disagreement branching differ from retaining only correct branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It doesn&#x27;t filter by outcome; success-only changes distribution after sampling. Preserve teacher scoring, termination supervision and matched cost/provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed branches still expose visited states; don&#x27;t remove them for prettier scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-773ea46ef6380052">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9191245083f7512a">Why not count shared BranchOPD prefix loss for every branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Added coverage is in suffixes. Deduplicate prefix and align valid positions. PBR supervises defined endings; boxed-then-EOS isn&#x27;t arbitrary early stop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five branches shouldn&#x27;t multiply unrelated early-token learning fivefold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9191245083f7512a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-boundary-evo-60ecea39" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4d4c905d8f2b6ca">Why reevaluate old BoundaryEvo problems each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student capability changes; mastered boundary questions should leave replay and new ones enter. Curriculum coevolves rather than replay static hard problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move to new gaps after mastering an old proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4d4c905d8f2b6ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7fd17e9fc0128f5">Why choose capability-boundary tasks then regenerate and verify teacher traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Value depends on current expert–student gap and old tasks need rechecking. Generate and verify anew to avoid carrying stale wrong answers. Priming and verified supervision have different rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retire mastered decompositions and validate the teacher&#x27;s new boundary solution instead of reusing an unchecked draft.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7fd17e9fc0128f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-835c2c91ce077e66">How does capability priming differ from verified teacher supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Priming is small-scale behavioral warmup without correctness filtering. Later select questions, generate fresh teacher responses and independently validate. Don&#x27;t present warmup as verified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Style imitation and checking a solution&#x27;s correctness use different acceptance rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-835c2c91ce077e66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e98dde6a3c689662">What must BoundaryEvo record before SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select tasks from current student/fixed expert/analyzer gap and quality, generate fresh verified teacher traces, and supervise only response tokens. No test references or old answers mislabeled fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A previous answer for another question breaks selection-to-supervision alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e98dde6a3c689662">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-recal-386ad741" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-84a60a24fbdb3407">Why account for recoverability before pruning in ReCal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Severe pruning can induce poor student states that distillation struggles to repair. Probe damage informs channel reselection toward recoverable structures instead of relying solely on later training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a key arithmetic path may not be fixed by simply distilling longer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84a60a24fbdb3407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8cc63e77f549c436">Why measure pruning damage on a probe but reselect channels on the unpruned model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe reveals harmed teacher states; use their damage to reweight original activations. This can avoid poor student trajectories that are hard to repair. Preserve remaining vocabulary mass in damage KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raise calibration weight on carry states harmed by the probe instead of patching already removed channels arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8cc63e77f549c436">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3fb80191720e2b7">How does damage-weighted calibration differ from activation-size pruning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe teacher states for damage, then reweight unpruned model statistics. Activation magnitude alone ignores recovery. Match target width and restoration protocol for fair comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare but badly damaged state can gain calibration weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3fb80191720e2b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3aa5afe4d1764d68">May ReCal drop probability outside teacher top candidates and renormalize?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep top events and remainder mass to estimate damage. Normalize response damage weights to unit scale; zero damage becomes uniform. Recompute selection from unpruned stats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Movement outside top tokens is invisible after local renormalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3aa5afe4d1764d68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pivot-65855e82" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-184154fc1deeefdf">Why switch PIVOT prompts to RL individually?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Students are not equally ready on all prompts. Uniform switching removes guidance too early for hard cases. Rank teacher perplexity on student replies and expand RL among low-perplexity prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let familiar tasks explore rewards while unfamiliar ones still distill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-184154fc1deeefdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4001ca700052909f">Why route low-perplexity problems to RL earlier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher support on actual student responses indicates readiness for reward exploration. High perplexity retains supervision; aggregate by prompt and ramp RL share. This isn&#x27;t a correctness or intrinsic difficulty test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch familiar teacher-supported steps sooner, while frequently divergent prompts continue distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4001ca700052909f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-02788785d8815ca5">Why aren&#x27;t teacher perplexity and verified correctness interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Perplexity measures teacher support for student wording, not task result. High support can be wrong and low support an effective novel route. It is a routing proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher unfamiliarity with phrasing does not make the conclusion false.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02788785d8815ca5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-17707b628c0a119d">How turn PIVOT response scores into problem routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponentiate each response&#x27;s mean teacher negative logp, average per prompt, standardize within batch and choose lowest via cosine proportion. Preserve separate GRPO/OPD normalizations, not token-level routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t decide a whole question from only its easiest completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17707b628c0a119d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-magicbeanstalk-9678e8db" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-32dc90312231b7d8">Why recursively decompose and compose MagicBeanStalk problems?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail hard tasks provide no advantage. Effective subproblem examples reveal dependency blueprints to synthesize new leaves and compose tasks with mixed current-policy outcomes. Valid format isn&#x27;t efficacy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Practice manageable parts and recombine them without losing key dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32dc90312231b7d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c26137f6ce5272c">Why can&#x27;t subproblem effectivity replace final Goldilocks selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parent improvement checks decomposition on one learner. Final task must not be all-correct or all-wrong under target budget and needs normally completed correct trace. Local teacher probes don&#x27;t complete recursive construction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Helpful subproblems for one student do not make a composed task learnable if target never solves it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c26137f6ce5272c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3edb9a183c7f314b">What do subproblem effectivity and target-policy Goldilocks each verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Effectivity asks if subexamples improve a student&#x27;s parent success. Goldilocks requires mixed outcomes and at least one normally terminated success under target budget. One doesn&#x27;t replace the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An auxiliary learner may improve while target still fails every final sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3edb9a183c7f314b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-41efd4ef1614f2c5">Can a well-formed local MBS problem be considered accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Need complete correct solution, independent validation, blueprint/novelty and effectivity/Goldilocks checks. Retain real construction failures; isolated teacher diagnostics aren&#x27;t acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid JSON and dependencies do not rescue an unsolvable task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41efd4ef1614f2c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grpo-dropout-a03001b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94cea1800fc90264">Why drop some high-probability positive-advantage replies in GRPODropout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
