<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They can oversharpen common modes. Selectively drop by entropy contribution while retaining failures. It isn&#x27;t neuron dropout and doesn&#x27;t refund generated rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reinforce fewer repeats of a common successful template.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94cea1800fc90264">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-880cfa0b36ab4eb7">Why filter high-probability positives but retain all nonpositives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant successes can further reduce entropy; select by entropy contribution, not random removal. Preserve negative learning and recenter with old probabilities. Generation cost is already paid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Downweight repeated successful templates without turning failures into omitted feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-880cfa0b36ab4eb7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ca549af2d7ba6d5">How does response dropout differ in cost from generating fewer replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate full group then filter updates; fewer samples would reduce generation and coverage, changing estimator. Less backward work isn&#x27;t equal end-to-end savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using six of eight generated replies does not cost only six generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ca549af2d7ba6d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ddbbf23888330984">Can GRPODropout keep original centered advantages after filtering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Restore all nonpositive samples and recenter retained ones by old-policy probability. Dropping either condition changes feedback/baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing strong positives shifts the reference and requires recentering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ddbbf23888330984">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dial-opd-c9cdfa1a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5413860493b450f1">Why multiply DIAL-OPD log gaps by logarithmic probability mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokens near impossible under both models can have large log differences. Scaling downweights such noise and prioritizes supported disagreements. Selection is not verifier truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bizarre word differing tenfold may matter less than a small gap on a key digit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5413860493b450f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c592ae65b12af48c">Why not select solely by largest teacher–student logp gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Huge gaps can occur in negligible mass. Logarithmic probability mean rescales priorities. Keep masked tokens as context; sparse supervision does not reduce generation or prove errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unlikely odd word should not drown out disagreement on a realistic key step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c592ae65b12af48c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ea92af295c46f6f">How does sparse DIAL supervision differ from deleting unselected text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unselected tokens stay as context but have masked losses. Removing text changes later prefixes and teacher scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep preceding arithmetic/connectives even when not training their tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ea92af295c46f6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5031e3253e24536">How handle equal p and q in DIAL&#x27;s logarithmic mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use its continuous limit. Choose each response&#x27;s own valid-position quota, detach advantages and differentiate final student logp only. Global ranking can let long answers dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal probabilities have a finite limit, not NaN or an arbitrary large score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5031e3253e24536">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lesser" data-paper-title="LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lesser-18cdf418" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5e873d09446feea">Why use output-layer gradients as LESSER selection features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alesser">LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full per-example backprop is costly. Independent readout gradient follows analytically from prediction residual and final hidden state in one forward, then project for the existing selector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep query similarity selection but replace expensive gradient features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03702">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03702-lesser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5e873d09446feea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lesser" data-paper-title="LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-23f6b957f56de63e">Why isn&#x27;t one-forward analytic output gradient an exact full-model substitute?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alesser">LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The outer product is exact for an independent readout; shared bilateral projection compresses it for existing selection. Tied embeddings can introduce indirect gradients. Use validation proxies and isolate test. This is not all-layer gradient equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select training examples using readout gradients of validation queries, not test examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03702">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03702-lesser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23f6b957f56de63e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lesser" data-paper-title="LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f265bae522721287">Is LESSER fully equivalent to full-model gradient similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alesser">LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exactness applies to an independent output layer; tied embeddings add hidden-state paths. Projection also approximates geometry and downstream performance needs testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar final-layer directions do not guarantee similar middle-layer updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03702">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03702-lesser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f265bae522721287">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lesser" data-paper-title="LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d424b130e8a7aebb">Why share random projections between LESSER candidates and queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alesser">LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only shared coordinates support comparison. Project both residual and hidden sides without materializing the full outer product. Use validation query proxies, never test selection; local random tensors are diagnostics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Independent projection draws per sample destroy comparability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03702">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03702-lesser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d424b130e8a7aebb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:follow-the-winners" data-paper-title="Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-follow-the-winners-b5a02f54" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d44fcdf056fedcaa">Why doesn&#x27;t FTW need same-prompt groups or a critic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Afollow-the-winners">Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Trent AI Limited</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stateful tool trajectories are expensive. Repeatedly draw minibatches from recent real FIFO traces, imitate within-batch elites and apply KL. Replay ranks replace some group sampling/value needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One trace per task can still participate in a pool minibatch tournament.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03361">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03361-follow-the-winners/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d44fcdf056fedcaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:follow-the-winners" data-paper-title="Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-410d39abbd09bc56">Why repeatedly select small-batch elites rather than pool top-K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Afollow-the-winners">Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Trent AI Limited</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random minibatches followed by local top reward yield smoothed occupancy, with repetition weighting. Hard global elites are a special case and may drop useful runners-up. No same-prompt groups/critic needed, but KL remains and local tool gains aren&#x27;t proven.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strongest often wins but a runner-up can win some batches; don&#x27;t deduplicate then equally weight them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03361">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03361-follow-the-winners/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-410d39abbd09bc56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:follow-the-winners" data-paper-title="Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d5e36608da4db56">Why aren&#x27;t repeated minibatch elites equivalent to one global top-K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Afollow-the-winners">Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Trent AI Limited</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated batches create soft rank occupancy; near-elites sometimes win. Global hard truncation retains only top ranks. Repeated selection counts are weights, so deduplication changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A second-tier trajectory can win a batch without the strongest opponents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03361">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03361-follow-the-winners/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d5e36608da4db56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:follow-the-winners" data-paper-title="Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d6b4047412aaba8">What are FTW limits K=C and C=N?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Afollow-the-winners">Follow the Winners: Conservative Policy Improvement with the Cross-Entropy Method for Critic-Free RFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Trent AI Limited</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>K=C keeps the whole sampled minibatch and yields uniform sampling. C=N draws the whole pool and yields global elites. Verify normalized distribution and preserve repeated selections; bandits aren&#x27;t tool-world results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If K=C still favors highest rank, the implementation misses the limit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03361">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.03361-follow-the-winners/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d6b4047412aaba8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dars-eb9dd187" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f737fb5a8ac8ba71">Why represent DARS progress as a dependency predicate graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars">Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Completed steps can rely on later-invalid conditions. Graph validation, invalidation and repair update related credit without clearing independent branches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Canceling a booking can affect itinerary but not unrelated document preparation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01207">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01207-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f737fb5a8ac8ba71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-644835722eac59bb">Why decay nearby credit rather than reset every completed step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars">Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Invalid prerequisites affect dependent branches, not independent work. Graph-distance decay and potential differences encode breakage/repair. Valid predicates and edges are prerequisites; local transitions aren&#x27;t agent gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ticket failure weakens hotel credit but not independent reimbursement materials.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01207">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01207-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-644835722eac59bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-680896d0dd51adf2">How does dependency-distance decay differ from global failure penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars">Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decay depends on relation to the broken prerequisite; global penalty ignores it. Wrong graph or predicates still misassign credit, so validate them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Flight-dependent hotels are affected, not unrelated account verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01207">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01207-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-680896d0dd51adf2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dars" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-985f17937ae96c42">Does DARS repair change only immediate reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adars">Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Update dependency state/potential and derive reward from differences. Otherwise later credit uses stale breakage. Local state kernel doesn&#x27;t train paper model; upstream interfaces aren&#x27;t released training code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repaired flights restore downstream state rather than add an isolated bonus.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01207">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2610.01207-dars/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-985f17937ae96c42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gats-23ea5c63" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dae826119dc52c7">Why lower GATS teacher weight as the student closes the gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher gives direction early under sparse rewards, but near a fixed reference it can restrict independent exploration. Permanently withdraw at the target and continue reward training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After reaching teacher-level success, continued imitation may hinder improvements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dae826119dc52c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f584461fdb668a3b">Why lag GATS success and permanently withdraw after catching teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lag avoids same-batch feedback and fixed benchmark stabilizes comparison. Linearly reduce distillation as gap closes, then keep teacher off despite fluctuations. Noise remains and only state machine was validated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An improvement affects guidance next batch; reaching benchmark isn&#x27;t a reversible toggle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f584461fdb668a3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7be6d244589f428f">How does permanent withdrawal differ from switching per batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Permanent state avoids oscillatory recalls; dynamic switching can restore help after a drop. Noisy pass rates mean reaching target once isn&#x27;t universal superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A slight later decline won&#x27;t restart teacher calls by design.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7be6d244589f428f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3efcce80c343cefb">Why use one-step-lagged EMA and fixed teacher tail success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current rewards cannot alter their own schedule. Fixed teacher baseline defines gap; handle zero baseline. Only schedule kernel, not Qwen agent RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log current batch then let next batch read updated EMA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3efcce80c343cefb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ross" data-paper-title="ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ross-56261390" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-53158c924443c142">Why reuse historical self-rollout in ROSS without imitating all of it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aross">ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team（原文以团队署名，未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old traces contain mistakes/redundancy. Full context conditions later behavior; selective continuation labels retain only valuable segments. Visible text need not be target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read the failure history but supervise only its selected correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35954">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35954-ross/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53158c924443c142">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ross" data-paper-title="ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9faad04c9357c685">Why retain full context but supervise selected continuation only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aross">ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team（原文以团队署名，未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History determines what state the continuation addresses. Masked supervision avoids imitating mistakes/redundancy while keeping context visible. Fixed local masks do not implement the paper selector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early error can remain visible while only a later successful repair is learned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35954">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35954-ross/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9faad04c9357c685">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ross" data-paper-title="ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-138dd71554ebd473">How does ROSS differ from deleting unselected spans before SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aross">ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team（原文以团队署名，未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deletion changes conditional state, while full context plus masked loss preserves the trace. Selector quality still matters; mask correctness is not selector implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a wrong prefix can change meaning/likelihood of a corrective sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35954">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35954-ross/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-138dd71554ebd473">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ross" data-paper-title="ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18dbcba85610e737">Is the local ROSS selector learned?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aross">ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team（原文以团队署名，未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A fixture mask verifies full-context/selective-loss boundaries, not autonomous selection of useful historical steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Marking the last two sentences manually tests adherence, not discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35954">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35954-ross/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18dbcba85610e737">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:roft" data-paper-title="Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-roft-6e694561" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7af0302d79d9d6da">Why turn environment feedback into retrospection before ROFT learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroft">Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal reward rarely expresses reusable lessons. Text reflections summarize useful experience from successes/failures. The reflection is the target, not every historical action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A permission mistake can teach checking access before next time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35741-roft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7af0302d79d9d6da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:roft" data-paper-title="Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa5d3a606524d353">Why supervise only retrospection tokens, not actions or feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroft">Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History conditions the lesson, but the target is the later reflection. Separate input and loss masks and globally average reflection tokens. Local fixtures/registry aren&#x27;t a complete agent/Evolve loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a bad call and error, but learn the parameter-check lesson, not the bad call or tool error text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35741-roft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa5d3a606524d353">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:roft" data-paper-title="Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd724cac5d5c8bf5">How does ROFT differ from cloning original actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroft">Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cloning repeats recorded behavior; reflection supervision can teach avoiding it. Different labels and reflection quality still matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After deleting a wrong file, learn to check paths rather than repeat deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35741-roft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd724cac5d5c8bf5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:roft" data-paper-title="Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3fe3fffdba6ba97">How normalize losses across differently sized ROFT retrospections?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroft">Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average all valid reflection tokens globally. Keep tasks/actions/observations/feedback as context but mask their loss. Per-reflection means change length weights. No full agent data/Evolve loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Short and long reflections contribute different total mass under token vs example means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35741">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.35741-roft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3fe3fffdba6ba97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-retire-opd-e8a79255" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c0fd08faf333c24">Why make RetireOPD teachers skill-specific and retirable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mastery varies. Retire when student approaches skill teacher and distribution improvement stalls, then explore with RL. Fixed uniform budgets can overteach known skills and underteach weak ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search and output format can retain different guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c0fd08faf333c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ad55afe94098476">Why not retire every teacher once overall student success is close?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each skill checks both outcome closeness and gap no longer shrinking. One criterion risks early withdrawal. Local mechanism checks don&#x27;t reproduce paper teacher training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search may qualify while formatting still lags; one total score can&#x27;t retire both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ad55afe94098476">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da2dbe2a3dc8b6d6">Why use both success and distribution gap for retirement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar success can leave valuable behavior differences. A stalled gap can occur despite low success. Joint thresholds estimate remaining teaching value, not universal teacher surpassing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching task scores alone don&#x27;t show tool choices stopped improving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da2dbe2a3dc8b6d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfc0702f7f16fe11">Do local retirement conditions show actual decoupled teachers were trained?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only retirement state and student update kernel. Log skill identity, success, gap trends and state; registry labels aren&#x27;t multi-teacher training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A synthetic retired state tests a branch, not genuine replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfc0702f7f16fe11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-trajectory-learnability-8d70d16c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44335d5c4b2a60d2">Why isn&#x27;t trajectory learnability just success reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success describes outcome, whereas current student mastery determines learning value. Token likelihood changes between successful reference and current policy reweight offline traces for remaining opportunity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct solutions can differ because student already knows one and misses the other&#x27;s key step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44335d5c4b2a60d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-16034fc631f8fda0">Why compare token likelihoods rather than rank offline traces by reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success alone doesn&#x27;t locate learning opportunities. Train reference on successes and compare likelihoods to current policy to estimate learnability. Depends on reference and offline coverage; local kernel only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweight two correct traces differently when one is mastered and the other has a difficult turning point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16034fc631f8fda0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72e52209edf16fe9">How does offline reweighting differ from collecting fresh on-policy data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight allocates budget inside existing coverage. New sampling reaches new states. OPD in the name doesn&#x27;t make replay current-policy generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweighting a cache cannot create an absent solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72e52209edf16fe9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67fb24ffbb9c3b16">Does local learnability aggregation include full GPU training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements token aggregation and trajectory weighting. Score identical text/prefix under both versions and record them; don&#x27;t subtract different responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old model scoring A and current model scoring B confounds text change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67fb24ffbb9c3b16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-growmtp-d690b374" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43adec038dd6f353">Why grow draft heads during RL in GrowMTP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Main policy evolves, making static drafters stale. Train multi-token heads with rollout acceptance to follow policy. Faster drafting isn&#x27;t task capability improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If policy learns new phrasing, drafter should propose it to retain acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43adec038dd6f353">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-49cc4453c625bc11">Why train by actual accepted depth and detach from backbone gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later drafts only contribute after earlier acceptance, so observed depth reflects use. Decoupling protects reward learning. Hardware and verification costs determine actual speed; local loss isn&#x27;t acceleration or capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third draft token isn&#x27;t as reachable as first, and improving it doesn&#x27;t prove stronger policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49cc4453c625bc11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e14ddb8dfe5131f8">How does acceptance-depth learning differ from equal future-head supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A later head helps only after earlier proposals are accepted. Depth coupling reflects use, unlike equal head contributions. Still verify with target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Head three saves a step only if the first two proposals pass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e14ddb8dfe5131f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-16c4706125d30fb6">Why decouple GrowMTP gradients, and was speed measured?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep draft optimization from inadvertently changing main RL objective. Local code tests acceptance-depth loss only, without measured GPU throughput. End-to-end speed needs timing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More accurate drafting may also add compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
