</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stride-opd-55204229" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ab8a5185b1e6dcf">Why restart STRIDE-OPD from the weakest correct turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cached learnable state focuses budget on barely mastered turns rather than regenerating familiar prefix. Correct qualification ensures a valid starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retry from a second turn that only just succeeds once the first is stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ab8a5185b1e6dcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfb066e0ae31243d">Why pair early stopping and restart from weakest correct turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher cumulative confidence avoids spending on low-value continuations. A weak but correct cached turn reassigns budget to practice. These are distinct choices, not jumps to gold. No real-model throughput validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stop an uninformative continuation, then retry from an earlier barely successful turn rather than repeatedly replay the familiar beginning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfb066e0ae31243d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5cd1beecf336df0">How does early stopping differ from uniform truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher cumulative confidence triggers a state-dependent stop paired with prefix restart. A fixed length limit changes coverage differently; shortness doesn&#x27;t guarantee completion or savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A solved trace and exploratory trace need not stop at the same token count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5cd1beecf336df0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-857ce14c8b27797d">Can STRIDE restore any environment from cached prefix text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align cached prefix with executed actions and observations. Text alone may omit environment state. Local state machine isn&#x27;t LLM rollout throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not duplicate a tool side effect on restore and call it the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-857ce14c8b27797d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-df-opd-48f2c181" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-152303e6ac1faa65">What dependency does data-free OPD reduce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher-generated prompts reduce collection of a separate post-training problem bank. Teacher knowledge and sampling still provide information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can create exercises without a human bank using existing learned skills.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-152303e6ac1faa65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cad6ac56bf666ca8">Why isn&#x27;t self-generated data-free OPD independent of prior knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher parameters, sampling and filters determine curriculum even without a separate task bank. Generated tasks can be repetitive/unreliable. Local diagnostics have not generated a natural-language dataset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating code exercises avoids human curation but repeated loop problems do not teach omitted concurrency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cad6ac56bf666ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d4419882e5e88b9">How does generated curriculum trade off with fixed public tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generated tasks can target teacher skills but repeat or omit topics. Fixed banks have auditable coverage and collection cost. Validate quality; linguistic format isn&#x27;t task validity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher repeating linear equations does not cover geometry automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d4419882e5e88b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-75cbfa58aed85ace">Has local DF-OPD generated a real natural-language training set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only policy-feature diagnostics for generated questions. Need actual generation, filtering and distillation provenance, not changing candidate indices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A feature ID isn&#x27;t a verified math problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75cbfa58aed85ace">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-locus-5c47d1f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27a97fe3f318d1e5">Why constrain LOCUS updates to task-related low rank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compact directions can improve token efficiency while limiting unrelated drift. If subspace misses key skills, performance can suffer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing redundant language may not require unrestricted changes to all parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27a97fe3f318d1e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1bbb645213174e0">Why can task-related low-rank updates shorten responses without truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learning operates on parameter directions and aims to preserve task-relevant changes. Truncation deletes content afterward, potentially essential. Validate subspace, correctness and efficiency; proxy SVD isn&#x27;t LLM evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn to omit redundant checks, not cut the second half of every proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1bbb645213174e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-00d679c76eed8a3e">How does low-rank learning differ from truncating output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Train more concise behavior rather than deleting already generated steps. Check correctness alongside length, not shorter alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omitting repetition and cutting a proof&#x27;s conclusion both shorten text but differ in quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00d679c76eed8a3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1961e19bf470995">Does local LOCUS SVD train a real language model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It projects policy gradients in a feature subspace. Check rank, orthogonality and gradient paths. A random low-rank matrix isn&#x27;t learned semantic direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Projection success doesn&#x27;t establish coverage of core reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1961e19bf470995">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-adaptive-opd-gate-493b3a1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0835105825885790">Why combine multiple signals for adaptive OPD gating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Entropy, uncertainty, reference drift and teacher/student gap capture different conditions. Combine them to allocate per-token forward/reverse KL; signal utility must be validated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher confident but far from reference differs from uncertain but close to student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-57b792891db90d75">Why mix FKL and RKL per token rather than select one direction per answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uncertainty, gaps and reference drift vary by token. Allocate coverage and concentration accordingly. Gate is a supervision heuristic, not truth, and local tests don&#x27;t show stable superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve multiple options at a pivotal branch and use concentrated guidance for settled format.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57b792891db90d75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae53784d12de3186">How does per-token FKL/RKL differ from one ratio per reply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token gates vary coverage vs concentration by position; fixed mixture applies everywhere. Flexibility increases tuning/overfit risk; diagnostics aren&#x27;t consistent wins.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reasoning branch and predictable format token need not receive the same mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae53784d12de3186">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4d08eed3b9a498f">Can local four-signal gates qualify for capability promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic mechanism tests don&#x27;t establish full-model effects or fair compute. Specify direction, signal versions and gradients; registry changes are not training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One improved small-candidate score doesn&#x27;t generalize to open language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sparse-opd-2b68a2ae" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4e9c98cacdbf422">Why study supervision at one or two positions in Sparse OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense supervision may be redundant. Select important positive teacher–student differences to test concentration of useful information. A particular experiment doesn&#x27;t prove one token suffices universally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correcting one operator can matter more than imitating many connectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4e9c98cacdbf422">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6859f74d2d04207">Why retain full context while supervising only a few largest positive gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher distributions depend on actual preceding reasoning. Sparse gradients don&#x27;t remove conditioning. Limited-position gains are setup-specific, and no local full-parameter distillation was run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score one key correction with prior calculations intact; deleting the prefix changes the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6859f74d2d04207">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-464fbb3a8d32673d">Why aren&#x27;t sparse loss and shorter generation the same efficiency improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse loss reduces supervised positions while keeping full trajectories and often scores them to find key tokens. Shorter generation changes cost and state coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating a thousand tokens and training one still pays for all generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-464fbb3a8d32673d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efb25fd7e2942129">How distinguish unselected-token gradients from context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unselected positions have no direct loss but stay as conditioning; shared weights may still affect them. Local candidate tests aren&#x27;t full Qwen/Llama training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omitting step two&#x27;s loss doesn&#x27;t allow deleting it before scoring step three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efb25fd7e2942129">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-specroll-077f92f9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2b6bdaeac9dff6c">Why use fast and slow draft adaptation in SpecRoll?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RL changes target policy. Lightweight hidden corrections handle short drift; persistent degradation triggers future-head training. Both improve proposals without replacing target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Quickly adjust a transient acceptance drop, retrain the head only if it persists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2b6bdaeac9dff6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d1234935a356567">Why can&#x27;t fast correction or slow draft-head training replace exact verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They improve proposals as policy evolves; exact rejection/acceptance preserves target distribution. Skipping it changes RL data even with a strong drafter. No local large-model throughput evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adapt the drafter after lag, but still verify every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d1234935a356567">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7efb0aba37ca861e">Does changing the SpecRoll draft change GRPO target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact target verification preserves sampling distribution, so GRPO stays unchanged. Skipping verification would change behavior data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Frequent correct drafts don&#x27;t make their probabilities target policy probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7efb0aba37ca861e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e3ea16b91f9a1ba">Does local SpecRoll registration prove large-model RL throughput?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only states and selection paths are checked. Real work needs acceptance/rejection residuals, scheduling and compute measurements; listing isn&#x27;t execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A listed candidate does not demonstrate complete GPU training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e3ea16b91f9a1ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rail-7f7d9ac0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c263ba6e6c66676d">Why learn recoverability rather than just uncertainty in RAIL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An uncertain state may be irreparable. Intervene based on expected recovery net of cost and condition on location/action, instead of uniformly spending extra.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One missing tool retry and a fundamentally wrong premise have different recovery value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c263ba6e6c66676d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b91768c570d659e">Why optimize intervention location/method with cost instead of oversampling uncertain states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Additional budget helps only recoverable states. Learn intervention-specific net gains from auditable shadow/live feedback as policy changes. Never use gold to decide; no local full environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One more tool call can rescue a trace while no reasonable budget repairs a false premise; entropy alone can&#x27;t tell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b91768c570d659e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc3188e5d5410b22">How does shadow-to-live evaluation differ from gold-based intervention choice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use permitted probes and actual feedback to learn recovery value. Gold would be an unavailable oracle. Deployment state must exclude training-only diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restarting from a known solution plan is an oracle diagnostic, not a learned controller.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc3188e5d5410b22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e56f84403d3fc865">What does the local RAIL path establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference intervention selection and cost objective, not the paper&#x27;s LLMs, private environment or judges. Execute and evaluate real recoveries before capability/budget claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Argmax over random recovery scores does not measure actual trajectory repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e56f84403d3fc865">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-coba-rl-1893eb3e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bebe79393c05758">Why use pass@k to probe CoBA-RL boundaries before teacher help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pass@1 can increase by concentrating old successes. Larger-budget coverage finds currently difficult reachable edges, where teacher guidance supplies new routes for RL consolidation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Occasional successes becoming frequent differs from learning a previously unseen solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bebe79393c05758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5709b23a4b1224c">Why inspect both pass@1 and larger pass@k for capability boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First-hit gain may just popularize known paths. Multiple samples probe coverage, then teacher and RL target boundaries. Finite budgets still miss rare paths; local small sampling does not reproduce high-k expansion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Measure whether once-never-solved prompts become reachable with broader sampling, counting teacher cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5709b23a4b1224c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-03ea6cc76d47837a">How does a boundary curriculum differ from ranking fixed textual difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reestimate from current policy samples; textual complexity doesn&#x27;t track mastery. Finite k can miss rare successes, so boundary depends on budget and isn&#x27;t impossibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long problem may leave the boundary after learning a new technique.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03ea6cc76d47837a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9daf279970f9b21e">Does local pass@8 establish paper pass@256 gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Teacher/student scales and sampling budgets differ. Genuine generation, triggers and cost curves support scaled mechanisms only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure in eight draws doesn&#x27;t imply failure after over 200 draws.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
