<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle-66732323" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbea5a3e23945c93">Why emphasize equal-label-budget stages in the sparse-to-dense reward principle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense teachers have different supervision costs. Match label budgets and stages to understand ordering. Contribution is an empirical four-stage comparison, not another KL function.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More teacher calls can improve scores without proving dense objectives caused the gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbea5a3e23945c93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a171a8da19e34101">Why isn&#x27;t the principle just sequencing GRPO and KL functions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper tests four stages under equal label budgets and distinguishes forward KL on teacher-visited states from reverse KL on student states. Operators alone don&#x27;t reproduce it. No local complete training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same KL name on a teacher solution and a student error refers to different supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a171a8da19e34101">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d26c9a44ab00a9cf">Is the same KL direction equivalent on teacher and student occupancy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Teacher ideal and student actual prefixes visit different errors. State source and divergence together define supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A KL on a correct proof and on a wrong intermediate state teaches different recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d26c9a44ab00a9cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d9196ac9cfedb73">Do existing GRPO and OPD operators reproduce the four stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Literature only; no full scheduling, real frozen teacher or equal-budget runs. Shared tokenizer and other prerequisites still matter. Stage labels aren&#x27;t execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Listing four configuration stages does not validate their data flow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d9196ac9cfedb73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lightning-opd-b1670874" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0e66c15fe51a1fd">Why cache Lightning OPD teacher scores before updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online teacher inference can bottleneck training. Score initial student traces once and reuse labels. This front-loads cost rather than eliminating generation/scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prepare teacher scores per prefix and reread them for multiple updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0e66c15fe51a1fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d662b69ce7015b40">Why isn&#x27;t cached teacher scoring equivalent to continuously online distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Initial student samples are scored under one teacher config. Later updates shift visitation without refreshing labels. Coverage and teacher consistency govern the cost tradeoff; local evidence is data flow only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cached early error prefixes help initially but later new approaches need an explicit refresh protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d662b69ce7015b40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4833bd93af00c6b0">How does offline cache coverage differ from refreshing rollouts each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cache covers initial student visits; updated policy may reach new states. Refreshing covers those at higher cost. Cached isn&#x27;t always on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newly learned solution&#x27;s prefixes won&#x27;t appear automatically in an old cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4833bd93af00c6b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dddd41106ab3d2b">What Lightning cache identities must match?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher checkpoint, prompt, tokenizer, response and position mask. Changes invalidate labels. Local data flow is not Qwen vocabulary distillation or AIME.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tokenizer update can misalign stored token scores despite the same filename.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dddd41106ab3d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cross-script-knowledge-transfer-cff708b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21884a7e420cd1b2">Why does cross-script knowledge research test more than translation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Another script can affect entity recognition, retrieval of parametric facts and reasoning expression. Translation is one factor. Regression/interventions separate them; this isn&#x27;t a new RL algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failing on a transliterated name doesn&#x27;t prove the model never learned facts about that person.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21884a7e420cd1b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ca85a2d8b44437e">Why doesn&#x27;t mechanical transliteration determine whether knowledge exists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Script changes can affect identity recognition, retrieval and expression, which before/after outputs cannot disentangle. The paper uses regression, training entity prompts and actual LoRA. Local reference notes are not capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure on a name in another script may be entity mismatch; hints diagnose but don&#x27;t establish transfer training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ca85a2d8b44437e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e434884eee2a2d72">Can inference transliteration replace training-time entity interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Training interventions study retrieval/learning pathways; transliteration changes current input and may bypass difficulty. String rules or a small classifier cannot stand in for LoRA and semantic transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalizing names to a familiar script can help without teaching cross-script transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e434884eee2a2d72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0480a7b8e8e475bc">Is there an executable local knowledge transfer operator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Literature only; real LM semantics and LoRA training are not implemented. Equations/generic SFT don&#x27;t imply reproduction, and prompts must not include test answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A working transliteration function is not the paper&#x27;s parametric retrieval mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0480a7b8e8e475bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-prompt-level-distillation-91a64214" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2a7d297d28d0a8c">Where does PLD store knowledge without parameter fine-tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher abstracts, clusters and revises readable system rules. A student uses frozen instructions at inference. Rules are learned artifacts despite unchanged weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Package date-processing lessons as system instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2a7d297d28d0a8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8e39103d977724f">Why separate train/validation/test without student weight updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Labeled examples shape rules through extraction, clustering and revision. They carry learned information. Validate and freeze, then never patch from test answers. PLD compiles reasoning into instructions, not parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Freeze date normalization after validation; adding a test-gold exception leaks even without gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8e39103d977724f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d97c7cd044405c08">How does semantic DBSCAN differ from string deduplication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cluster paraphrased micro-rules and filter noise rather than only exact repeats. Conflicts still require training-error revisions; lists don&#x27;t ensure consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Differently worded unit-conversion rules can share a cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d97c7cd044405c08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa6ed62dc42efca1">When freeze PLD rules, and can test feedback revise them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract/repair on train, use validation for convergence and freeze before test. Prompt changes can leak without weight updates; track versions/provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a test-specific date exception and rescoring is not independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa6ed62dc42efca1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-chord-f1e12f5e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-69baa45da687fd7d">Why anneal CHORD SFT auxiliary weight during RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert demonstrations stabilize early exploration; excessive later imitation can restrict it. Dynamic weighting and token uncertainty ease the handoff without abrupt shift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Begin with more standard examples, then let outcome reward guide increasingly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69baa45da687fd7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-751d193dd884b093">Why taper expert supervision instead of switching off SFT at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early guidance stabilizes exploration, but prolonged imitation constrains it. Annealing and uncertainty weights allow a gradual transition while monitoring source shift. Blending isn&#x27;t universally better; local proxy isn&#x27;t an uncertainty model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give learner less expert help as it improves rather than always equal help or an abrupt cutoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-751d193dd884b093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de0dc149fb4ad21f">Is CHORD the same as PIVOT&#x27;s per-question switching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. CHORD blends losses with annealed supervision; PIVOT routes prompts by teacher perplexity to separate objectives. Granularity and schedule differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One can apply both losses to a prompt; the other chooses its route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de0dc149fb4ad21f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4af7a15d2745480">Does local CHORD gold candidate model real token uncertainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic expert proxy; no LLM uncertainty model. Track expert off-policy vs student rollout and anneal as specified; keep expert answers out of evaluation inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed candidate labels don&#x27;t estimate uncertainty at every long-text position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4af7a15d2745480">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spiral" data-paper-title="SPIRAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-spiral-8df7f07c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c95c0c1a16fcba51">Why let one SPIRAL model propose and solve games?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspiral">SPIRAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An adversarial, decidable zero-sum game creates a curriculum as opponents evolve. Roles need distinct rewards and explicit rules; proposer cannot declare outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One role creates a position, another tries to solve it, and a program judges.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.24119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.24119-spiral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c95c0c1a16fcba51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spiral" data-paper-title="SPIRAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7816033509093ce3">Why require automatically decidable game rules in zero-sum SPIRAL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspiral">SPIRAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adversarial progress creates curriculum, but independent rules must decide wins. Zero-sum incentives do not guarantee broad reasoning coverage. Local state/objective checks don&#x27;t reproduce self-play training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The proposer can&#x27;t change rules midgame to make every solution lose.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.24119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.24119-spiral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7816033509093ce3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spiral" data-paper-title="SPIRAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8712f25147d80f3">What are limits of self-play vs fixed hard-problem banks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspiral">SPIRAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-play adapts but can get trapped in game-specific tricks. Fixed banks have defined coverage but no evolving opponent. Game gains don&#x27;t imply general reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Winning a word game needn&#x27;t improve math, retrieval or tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.24119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.24119-spiral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8712f25147d80f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spiral" data-paper-title="SPIRAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa88b77e42aae8aa">Why preserve zero-sum rewards across SPIRAL roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspiral">SPIRAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One outcome gives opposite credit under aligned states/rules. Rewarding both for the same victory changes the game. Local kernel isn&#x27;t large multi-round training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proposer win cannot also be a solver win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.24119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2506.24119-spiral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa88b77e42aae8aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-absolute-zero-7e819456" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-756d0db2f64d583b">Why does Absolute Zero still need an executable verifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generated tasks and solutions aren&#x27;t truth. Program execution provides independent reward. No human item labels isn&#x27;t no supervision; task executability and verifier quality bound scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Run generated code rather than trust its claimed output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-756d0db2f64d583b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97e862263943075f">Why does a self-generated Absolute Zero curriculum still need verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposer creates tasks, solver answers and program execution supplies independent rewards, replacing human annotations. Verifiable tasks still supervise; exposing saved answers breaks the loop. Local diagnostics aren&#x27;t full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate executable code and predict output, then run it to grade instead of showing stored stdout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97e862263943075f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1c625299ded1b0f">How does making harder tasks differ from a capability-boundary curriculum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Too hard can yield all failures and no signal. Use verifiable challenges near current ability. Legal format and novelty don&#x27;t establish teaching value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task no one can solve at the budget may be worse for learning than a moderate challenge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1c625299ded1b0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cba8bebbfe55e0e">Can Absolute Zero show solver answers saved during task generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep execution results on verifier side; solver sees public task only. Local curriculum/state checks aren&#x27;t large-model capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t append actual output to the program-output prediction prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cba8bebbfe55e0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:raft" data-paper-title="RAFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-raft-fe9d648c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b34e16004065fe4">Why keep generating fresh RAFT candidates from current policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Araft">RAFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed SFT data can&#x27;t follow improvement. Resample, rank by reward and supervise better behavior next round. Coverage still limits which outputs can be chosen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improved summarization can generate better candidates for later training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.06767-raft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b34e16004065fe4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:raft" data-paper-title="RAFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3b8808917c40363">How does reward selection followed by maximum likelihood differ from direct policy gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Araft">RAFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rank sampled replies with the reward model and supervise selected text; scores determine selection, not per-action gradient weights. Resample with the next policy. Judge bias and missing candidates persist; local tests cover the iteration state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn the highest-rated candidate summary; absent good summaries can&#x27;t be chosen and judge errors can be copied.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.06767-raft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3b8808917c40363">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:raft" data-paper-title="RAFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc21318c02d86430">How does reward enter RAFT differently from PPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Araft">RAFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RAFT uses reward to select texts and then applies maximum likelihood. PPO uses advantages and probability ratios directly in policy objective. Selection and continuous weighting differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high score can decide archive admission without proportionally increasing CE.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.06767-raft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc21318c02d86430">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:raft" data-paper-title="RAFT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd03d4197adb8876">How isolate RAFT selection from evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Araft">RAFT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · HKUST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log reward model and rollout version, select among same-prompt candidates then update policy. No test answers for sorting. Local candidates aren&#x27;t a real generator or reward model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training on choices made with test correctness invalidates held-out gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.06767-raft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd03d4197adb8876">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Should a limited budget buy more questions, more rollouts, or more supervision at valuable positions?

## Takeaway

Question selection changes visited states, curricula change difficulty, and trimming supervision or rollout reduces per-example cost. Difficulty estimates age as the policy improves. Separate data selection from target tasks and a fixed evaluation set. LESSER makes selection cheaper through output-layer gradient features; it does not replace the selection objective. Compare quality under the total budget and identify which step actually gets cheaper.

## Example

With 100 answers per day, more rollouts on solved questions may add little; unsolvable questions may provide no positive rewards. Re-estimate success on training data, sample the difficulty band with remaining signal, and retain a hard control. If rollouts end halfway, token inclusion probabilities change and the old unweighted objective may no longer apply.

## Common pitfall

Faster is not better learning and fewer tokens are not matched quality. Include teacher forward passes, question synthesis, screening, and retries in cost. Select curricula or budgets on validation and report isolated test. CPU gradient and clipping checks do not prove training speedup, and cross-script transfer research is not an executable optimizer.

## Reading order

Read GRPO Difficulty Curriculum for policy-dependent difficulty, LESSER for cheap gradient features versus selection rules, and STOPD for early stopping with explicit sampling and weighting.

1. [A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO](../../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669)
2. [LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients](../../../../post-training/2610.03702-lesser/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03702)
3. [Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?](../../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1)

## Check your understanding

Can we keep the previous round's “medium difficulty” label after the policy changes?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Not by default. Difficulty depends on the current policy and sampling budget. Re-estimate under the chosen curriculum using permitted training/validation information, not final test. If budget forces reuse, state that limitation; fixed prompt length is not success-probability difficulty.

</details>
